featured_reviews.name: nehaal peerbhoy
featured_reviews.review_text: Dr Kurush and Dr Dipti are simply excellent. My cat, golu was brought to them when his condition wasn't good at all. I had been to various veterinarians to treat golu and in the process spent an arm and a leg. Their diagnosis was on point and they took the right decision at each and every point based upon only my cat. They also went above and beyond in helping with having someone sent over to my house for my cats injections and I.v supplements. They were available on the phone whenever I called them during emergencies. They gave golu a fighting chance and I thank them for it. I've been to more vets than I can count and they were definitely the best. Dr Kurush might not be a people person( I don't find him rude at all) and he might be a bit direct at times but he's an excellent vet and I feel like the directness is what is required for pet owners. They charge far lower than all other vets and are very transparent and honest when it comes to their fees and charges.

featured_reviews.name: ananya roy
featured_reviews.review_text:
I only trust Dr. Dipti and Dr. Kurush with my cats.

I used to come all the way from Lower Parel to Marine lines for any emergency as well as regular checkups. I moved even farther away to Kurla, and still did not try to find any other vet.

They call a spade a spade, and care deeply about your pet's well being. While they are running a business, their instincts are guided by care for animals, rather than making money. No marketing. No gimmicks. Just healing the animal. 5 stars.

featured_reviews.name: Bharati Malar Periasamy
featured_reviews.review_text:
These are the doctors I would blindly trust with my pets. They put the patients first and the owners second, which in my opinion is the way to go. They will tell you straight up if you are inadvertently harming your pet with your routine. All they expect from you is that you follow their instructions, and not assume you know better. That is not much to ask for at the end of the day.
Super-dedicated and up-to-date with their treatments, skilled at various surgeries (the sutures are absolutely tiny!!), they still find the time to rescue & treat strays, and manage a household full of cats (both pets and rescues!) with no help.

Absolute stars, the both of them!

7-15 days after the operation, my dog started to have excessive and unstoppable nose bleeding and on having taken her to the Churchgate Petzone, and I remember waiting there what felt like an eternity just to get a doctor to attend to her and then came this young female doctor who behaved extremely rudely and clearly the only two doctors had no clue what do with my poor little pet who clearly was in pain. Then the next horror began when they started coordinating with their senior doctor over the phone and everythinf seemed like chaos for the next few hours! They decided to sedate her and my pet's bleeding finally stopped.

And after all this, nobody could tell us what actually had happened to my dog and the bleeding continued for the next few days too. Anyway, I never really took her there again because what's a clinic if you can't treat patients calmly in an emergency! featured_reviews.review_text:
I had a wonderful experience with both Dr. Drona and Dr. Sarang, and I’m truly grateful for the care they provided to my pet, Loki.

Dr. Sarang has always been extremely kind, patient, and receptive. He never hesitated to clear my doubts and always took the time to explain everything in detail whenever I was worried. It makes a huge difference when your vet is not only knowledgeable but also genuinely caring. I also really appreciate the fitness-to-travel certificate he provided for Loki, a very kind gesture that meant a lot to me. Being a doctor myself, I understand how valuable time is, which makes his help even more appreciated.

Dr. Drona was also always very approachable and reassuring. He performed Loki’s surgery, and everything went smoothly. The procedure and recovery both went well, and I felt confident knowing Loki was in safe and experienced hands.

Overall, I’m very thankful to both of them for their dedication, skill, and kindness. Highly recommend them to anyone looking for trustworthy and compassionate veterinary care.

featured_reviews.name: Armaan Bhatia
featured_reviews.review_text:
I went with my cat there, she had some internal problem related to birth of a premature baby done at a young age, I take the blame on me for not taking her to the hospital on time, but whatever I've experienced there was no less comforting. I'll write the start to finish of what I've seen and experienced.

•The greeting:
At gate they ask you for ₹10, still okay as they let you go in first and look for payment later. Although when I admitted my cat, they asked for more for their "chai nashta" Which isn't necessary as she's a part of the ward.

•Ward:
I don't know about any other ward personally, but for CATS, there are 4 wards(wardA, B, C & D), my cat was in ward D, and it wasn't "comfortable for patient" type. They have cages in a room on which they lay a sheet of diaper and keep your cat with food and water. And if they don't have diapers, they'll make them lay on the cage's floor which is a welcome for the cat to catch cold. Plus there were red ants in the cage, and the hygiene wasn't up to mark, specially for cats who have cuts that can get maggots or infections in them due to such a rest place

•The Medical Ward:
They have only 4 tables/stretchers for Animals, alot less for a hospital so big.

1) The medical ward is mostly filled with ward boys, the people who have the job to LOOK AFTER PATIENTS in the WARD.

2) There are 1-2 main doctors, in which One of them was constantly sitting on his chair while the substitute/junior doctors came over to ask him for what to do. It was more looked like a biology class where students were asking the teacher for help.. WHILE ANIMALS WERE FIGHTING FOR LIFE. The second doctor was helpful, he was treating animals which I'll praise him for.

3) The ward boys, despite being more than 15 there, weren't taking the MOMENT seriously. They were actively talking, joking, hanging around as if they're in a park. And if you have a pet waiting to be treated with a table empty infront of you, the ward boy won't even look at you, he would instead go somewhere and just stand, clearly showing he Is currently free but not helping.

4) note, the medical ward is ONLY open between 10:00 - 13:00.

5) while they were injecting my cat, instead of focusing on her, they were actively talking. My cat even went under a shock where she almost died but was recovered.

6) while taking her blood for blood test, the doctor squeezed her leg(from where they took the blood) to get samples, It's understandable as she got skinny due to the lack of food and water, but after the work, they didn't massage or rubbed the part of the leg to losen the squeezed muscle down. Because of which, 10 minutes after keeping her in a basket, I noticed her leg being stained by her blood.

•Treatment of a passed away body:
When I reached hospital after hearing my cat's loss, I looked for her in the ward, medical room, etc. When I asked someone, he took me to a room where my cat's body was kept in a pull-away trolley with a dusty rug kept over her. As a animal parent, I can't see my cat's body being kept like trash, Atleast keep her on the hoodie I provided, idc if she doesn't feel the comfort anymore, but that'd atleast give me a relief that she had my presence around her until her last breath.

Note: I take responsibility for the death of my cat, im not saying that they allegedly kill them. My point is, where a human patient would usually get full care for even a small wound, the animals on other hand aren't given that much. The hygiene and prioritizing style of the hospital isn't quite much. It's almost as they don't take the animal as a living being. It's a decent hospital, but keep your beloved there at your own risk.

All we knew was that we needed the right oncologist — someone we could trust completely. That’s when we found the incredible team at Superpets, and from that very first visit, everything began to feel a little lighter.

From explaining the diagnosis and possible causes, to guiding us through every test, every step was handled with so much patience, clarity, and compassion. What truly stood out was how reassuring the entire team was — always available to answer questions, clear doubts, and take that extra effort to make both us and Goldie feel comfortable.

The journey — from diagnosis, to surgery, to post-operative care and stitch removal — was smoother than we could have ever hoped for. Every decision they made felt right, thoughtful, and in Goldie’s best interest.

A special note of gratitude to Dr. Pratyush, Dr. Vasudha, and Dr. Gauri — you are truly angels in disguise. The care, dedication, and gentleness with which you handled Goldie means the world to us. It’s not just medical expertise, but your genuine love for animals that makes all the difference.

This entire experience has been a journey of gratitude. People like them are not just treating animals — they are healing families.

Thank you, Superpets team, from the bottom of my heart, for taking such beautiful care of our baby.

Forever grateful. 🙏🏻

Despite this, the doctor continued giving injections on every visit and instructed us to administer them twice daily for an entire month.

Our concerns were ignored, and the same bandaging was continued at every visit. Instead of improving, the wound worsened drastically and became almost four times larger.

During dressing, we witnessed the originally small wound enlarged and develop a deep internal hole, which was extremely distressing as pet owners.

We also raised concerns about breathing issues, but no tests or treatment were provided for this either.

On one visit, we waited over an hour for the doctor while he was busy discussing charges for another patient with the another doctor. We clearly observed him indicating by hand signs whether to charge ₹9,000 or ₹10,000, after which ₹10,000 was decided. This gave us a strong impression that financial matters were being prioritized over patient care.

We expected timely diagnosis, proper wound management, transparency in treatment, and genuine concern for our pet’s health. Unfortunately, none of this was provided. We are deeply disappointed and would not recommend this vet based on our experience.

If you love your pet, please do not go here. Do not trust this vet.

featured_reviews.name: rishi basu
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its common knowledge that finding a genuine vet who actually cares and treats correctly is like finding a needle in a haystack. So when our go-to vet was unavailable and he recommended Central vets, the only question we asked was would you trust them with your pet.

So, I got my beagle Oshie to them for a suspected case of pyometra. Dr Patil did the USG and immediately confirmed the diagnosis. Oshie was rushed to surgery the next morning and hysterectomy was performed. It was a complicated  surgery but under the skilled hands of dr Patil, Oshie came out unscathed. But unfortunately, the worst was yet to come.

The next day she started showing unusual symptoms and upon rushing her to Dr patil, he confirmed that the toxins had spread in her blood stream resulting in Septecemia, an almost-always fatal disease.

Dr Patil and Dr Shelar lost no time in getting her into an aggressive line of treatment and for the most critical 48 hours, they made sure that Oshie got nothing but their full attention.

Once our vet was back then we took her for further treatment, but even then, they kept a track of how she was doing and kept checking up. In my all the years of having pets, i saw this empathy at a vet for the second time. (first being our go-to vet)

About the clinic: The clinic is very modern, well equipped and managed by an efficient team of ladies who i found quite pleasant to deal with. Even the young assistants were so caring and patient. They were all animal lovers and put each pet patient and their parents at ease.

The two doctors, Dr Patil and dr Shelar, are god-send. I will recommend Central Vets in a heart-beat. My Oshie is back with me and that is all due to their efforts.

God bless you worthy doctors and the entire team at Central Vets. Thank you from the bottom of our heart!

Love. Oshie, Mome and Rishi Basu

featured_reviews.name: Purna Parmar
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you’re an invested pet parent like me, this review might help you make an informed choice for your pet and yourself:

I first came across Central Vets (I'll use 'CV' from here on) through a cat rescuer friend, who told me something that really shocked me: most vets vaccinate cats in the wrong spots, which can cause a rare but dangerous condition. She said only the doctors at CV not only vaccinate in the correct spots, but also note it down (I had never seen that at any clinic in Mumbai - even the fancy ones) on the records which they hand over to you for your documentation. That alone made me want to try CV, and it’s been 3 years now.

Since then, Dr. Patil has become our doctor. As a pet parent, every single decision about your pet’s health - food, water, medicine, treatment, when, how much, how little,... - feels like it rests on you. One mistake and the responsibility is yours. That’s why finding someone you can fully trust is so important. For us, that’s Dr. Patil. We blindly trust his advice.

But it’s not just Dr. Patil - Dr. Shelar and the whole team are equally gentle, professional, and caring. At other clinics, it used to take 3–4 people to pin my 3kg cat down just to check her weight or give her a tablet. At CV, she often comes out of the carrier on her own, and even on days when she’s stressed from the travel (we live a bit far), they patiently wait and use kind techniques. That matters so much to me.

Another big thing: hygiene. I’ve seen some top-rated clinics in Mumbai that are shockingly unhygienic. At CV, it’s always spotless. Plus, their new space makes it all the more better - it is not only bigger but also super clean, airy, and comfortable for pets. There's also plenty space to sit and pace around with your pet in the waiting area.

I’ll share one example: during the rains I couldn’t travel all the way to CV, so I gave in and visited a local vet for my cat’s ear infection. Big mistake. Not only was the place unhygienic, but she also ended up catching the flu there. We wasted money, she suffered, and I felt stressed and guilty. That same evening I called CV, Dr. Patil recommended an ear drop, and within 3 days she was already so much better. Later, when we could make a visit, we went in for her proper treatment. That’s when I realized trust is everything, and we blindly trust our doctor.

Another plus if you are cat lover!: CV also cares for strays! Their old clinic had a tomcat called Damodar, and now their new space has another sweetie hanging around (with his own litter box haha). But don’t worry, the hygiene never slips. The clinic is still super clean and safe.

Lastly, a special mention to the lady at the reception who manages calls, appointments, and queries. She’s always kind and efficient, and has often helped us connect with the doctors when we couldn’t make it to the clinic or when it was after hours.

In short, CV is our safe space, and we rank it 5⭐️ on all parameters. I've recommended it to my friends, acquaintances, and fellows from the cat parent community. If you genuinely care about your pet’s health and wellbeing, I can’t recommend them enough.
